evidence.quote: By statute, a pass-through entity is defined as a corporation that for the applicable tax year is treated as an S Corporation under IRC § 1362(a) [26 U.S.C. § 1362(a)], and a general partnership, limited partnership, limited liability partnership, trust, or limited liability company that for the applicable tax year is not taxed as a corporation for federal tax purposes under the state's check-the-box regulation.

notes:
Rhode Island's recurring entity-level levy on a default LLC is the annual charge of R.I. Gen. Laws § 7-16-67: a return is filed with the tax administrator and 'an annual charge shall be due' on that filing, and an LLC not treated as a corporation for federal income tax purposes 'shall pay a fee in an amount equal to the minimum tax imposed upon a corporation under § 44-11-2(e)'. That minimum is $400 for tax years beginning on or after 2017. The label is the statute's own - 'Annual charge' - and the Division of Taxation describes the same payment as 'a tax or fee equal to a minimum tax imposed upon a corporation currently equal to $400'. basis is flat: the charge is the fixed $400 figure, not a measure of the LLC's activity. firstYearExemption is false: the charge is due on the filing of the LLC's first return and the statute states no first-year waiver. The due date for a default LLC is on or before the 15th day of the fourth month following the close of the fiscal year (calendar-year LLCs: April 15; a separate March 15 return schedule applied to pre-2016 years).
collectedWithAnnualReport is false: root states.json carries annual_report_fee 52.5 for Rhode Island, the Secretary of State's annual report fee under § 7-16-66 (filed between February 1 and May 1 with the SOS), a separate payment with no tax to overlap. The annual charge is paid to the Division of Taxation on the LLC's own return.
stateIncomeTax: members owe Rhode Island personal income tax on their pass-through shares; the Division's own pages state the highest individual rate as currently 5.99%, and the statute's pass-through section withholds on nonresident members at that rate. A pass-through entity may elect, for tax years beginning on or after 2019, to pay the state tax at the entity level at 5.99% (R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-11-2.3); for tax years beginning on or after 2025 the state tax credit passed through to owners is 90% of the entity-level tax paid. The business corporation income tax itself (7% of net income under § 44-11-2(a)) applies to corporations, not to a default LLC, and is not part of this record.
